title: Multilingual Programs Professional Learning
before:
The Maine Department of Education supports public schools in providing high-quality, effective programs for multilingual learners. Differentiated and responsive professional learning opportunities support the efficacy of programs for multilingual learners and build sustainable pathways to systematically integrate language and content instruction and assessment.

Upcoming Events

Strengthening Instruction for Multilingual Learners

This project is one component of Maine's coordinated statewide efforts to implement the Literacy and Numeracy Action Plans, which together aim to strengthen instruction, build educator capacity, and close persistent achievement gaps across all student populations.

Check out the resources

WIDA Professional Development

The WIDA Core Learning Collection provides on-demand, research-based professional development to strengthen instruction for multilingual learners. 

Explore practical strategies and resources to support multilingual learners’ access to rigorous, grade-level content. WIDA Self-Paced Workshops may take up to four hours, while On-Demand Videos typically take less than one hour. Maine DOE-sponsored learning opportunities are available at no cost and can be used for individual professional learning or collaborative learning with colleagues and teams.

Offerings are available through the WIDA Secure Portal from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027.

notes: Heading levels skip: jumps h2 to h5. Needs a person.

decisions.label: Let very uneven cards find their own height
decisions.why: 1 row pairs a short card with one holding nearly three times as much. Equal heights stretch the short one and the difference reads as a hole, so these are allowed to sit at the height of what is in them.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 2 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 2 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Let a colon do its own work
decisions.why: A colon marks the words before it as a term and the words after it as what the term means. Here 1 list item opens with a term set in the same weight as its own explanation, so the list cannot be scanned. No word changes and nothing is removed.

decisions.label: Put the content under its own heading
decisions.why: "Upcoming Events" had nothing beneath it, and the content that belongs to it was written above the heading instead of below. Nothing is added or removed; it moves under its own title.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: The Maine Department of Education supports public schools in providing high-quality, effective programs for multilingual learners. Differentiated and responsive professional learning opportunities support the efficacy of programs for multilingual learners and build sustainable pathways to systematically integrate language and content instruction and assessment.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.
decisions.removes: Multilingual Learners - Professional Development Website Banner.png

decisions.label: Size an image by its shape
decisions.why: "Core Learning" measures 477×487 — it was sitting in the flow at its own pixel size, aligned with nothing.

decisions.label: Bring every heading up to h3 or above
decisions.why: 2 headings sat at h4 or deeper inside a card, a callout, a contact block or an accordion panel — components the outline walk leaves alone because they label a thing rather than a section. A reader using a screen reader still hears the level, so a fourth-level title inside a page that only goes to three is announced as belonging to a level that does not exist. Each is styled by its class and its position rather than its number, so nothing changes on screen.

decisions.label: Add a contents list (4 sections)
decisions.why: Built from the section headings already on the page. Below three sections a list is not a route.
